A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CountsDiff. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and renumbered tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-count experiments, CIFAR-10 and CelebA generation results, and fetal and heart scRNA-seq imputation experiments, including appendix ablations and classifier evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports expanded imputation comparisons and additional evaluation metrics in Tables 2, 3, 10, and Appendix E.6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.6 and Algorithms 1-2 retain the same forward process, weighted objective, attrition mechanism, guidance, stochastic rounding, and RePaint-based imputation. Expanded explanations and baseline implementation disclosures do not establish changes to CountsDiff itself.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic count vectors, CIFAR-10, CelebA, and the fetal and heart cell atlases. The fetal 50% MCAR and 25% low-biased MNAR tasks, heart 50% MCAR task, and fetal 40% MCAR ablations are retained. No additional evaluated dataset or missingness scenario is documented.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 10 add scGPT trained from scratch and pretrained, xTrimoGene, and Blackout to the full imputation comparisons. HI-VAE is now evaluated with both Poisson and Gaussian likelihoods. Blackout previously appeared in other experiments, but its participation in these comparisons is new; RAW is simply renamed Zero imputation.

E3.justification: The imputation benchmarks expand from four metrics to include ED, MMD, and SWD, with R-squared, MAE, and Pearson correlation added in Appendix E.6. GAIN's reported training budget changes from 50 epochs to 10,000 iterations. The splits and gene panels remain unchanged. V2 also inconsistently describes toy SWD as both Wasserstein-1 and Wasserstein-2, leaving any actual implementation change there unclear.

E4.justification: V1's scIDPMs comparison with and without catastrophic outliers disappears from Tables 3 and 10. V2 adds a limited scratch-versus-pretrained scGPT comparison. The rounding checks, schedule/guidance/attrition/sampling-step sweeps, and downstream classifier evaluation remain; the classifier study moves from Appendix E.6 to E.7.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean and standard error using ten resamples of 50,000 fetal or 20,000 heart data points; v2 explicitly calls these bootstrap resamples. No additional runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure are reported. Changed uncertainty values and display precision do not establish a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 10 revise numerous imputation scores and add substantial comparator and metric results. For fetal MCAR, single-sample CountsDiff RMSE changes from 1.401 to 1.42; GAIN changes from 51.163 to 1.87 alongside its revised reported setup. Newly added pretrained scGPT achieves MNAR RMSE 0.24. Toy, image, and existing ablation results are retained, apart from rounding.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.1, 3.2, and B.1 and the derivations in Appendix B are retained. Changes to mathematical presentation concern notation, punctuation, and typesetting, including explicit probability symbols in B.9, rather than new assumptions, proofs, or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: a clarified and extended count-diffusion design space, transferred guidance and attrition mechanisms, and competitive generation and biological imputation. Expanded evidence and revised result interpretations do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 now distinguishes pointwise prediction from distributional fidelity and acknowledges stronger pointwise competitors. It attributes foundation-model success on low-biased MNAR data to miscalibration, without testing the proposed high-biased counterexample. New Section 8 explicitly discusses sampling speed, limited exploration of design choices, restricted gene coverage, and unexplored biological adaptations.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the anonymous reviewer-code disclosure with a public repository link and expands Appendix D.3 substantially. It documents PyTorch GAIN/HI-VAE implementations, GAIN activation handling, a 100,000-step CountsDiff/ReMDM budget, scIDPM epoch counts within the retained 150-hour budget, and ED/MMD/SWD computation. Newly disclosed details do not by themselves establish changed experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning around scGPT, xTrimoGene, and few-step samplers, plus FID/IS references, while removing examples such as scVAE, AdImpute, and scDesign3. The central relationship to Blackout and JUMP remains unchanged. Numerous publication-year and venue updates refer to the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section order remain recognizable. V2 makes localized explanatory edits, numbers the experiment subsections, rewrites the imputation discussion, reorganizes Appendix D.3, and adds a dedicated limitations section. Affiliations and the publication header also change; most method and proof prose is retained.

P2.justification: The principal imputation tables are substantially redesigned with additional columns, pointwise/distributional headers, method groups, and within-group highlighting. V2 adds full-metric Tables 14-16, compresses Table 1, and integrates Figures 7-11 beside their appendix discussions instead of leaving them at the document's end. These relocated figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central biological evaluation through stronger comparators and multiple distributional metrics, reducing reliance on scFID and making CountsDiff's pointwise weaknesses explicit. Expanded implementation information, the public-code disclosure, and concrete limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. These gains outweigh remaining shortcomings: the new foundation-model settings are sparsely documented, and the explanation of their MNAR advantage remains untested.
